images.title: Diagonals at 60° still make right angles
images.purpose: Shows equal diagonals bisecting each other at 60°: the corner at A is made of 60° and 30°, which is 90°.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One upright rectangle in the centre with its diagonals crossing, the angles at the crossing and at one corner marked, and one short sum under the shape.
images.exact_structure: One rectangle ABCD in dark outline, taller than it is wide (height about 1.73 times the width), with A top left, B top right, C bottom right and D bottom left. The diagonals AC and BD are thick teal (#0072B2) lines crossing at O; each of the four half diagonals carries one identical short dark tick mark. At O, inside the top triangle AOB, a small amber (#E69F00) arc labelled 60°; at O, inside the left triangle AOD, a larger amber arc labelled 120°. At corner A two small reddish purple (#CC79A7) arcs: one between the top side AB and the diagonal AC labelled 60°, and one between the left side AD and the diagonal AC labelled 30°. Under the rectangle, centred, the line 60° + 30° = 90°. Only corner A is lettered: the letter A sits just outside the top left corner; the other corners carry no letters. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Equal diagonals that bisect each other make every corner 60° + 30° = 90°, so the shape is a rectangle.
images.description: Shows equal diagonals bisecting each other at 60°: the corner at A is made of 60° and 30°, which is 90°.
images.context: ∆AOB has OA = OB and 60° at O, so base angles (180 − 60) ÷ 2 = 60; ∆AOD has 120° at O, so base angles (180 − 120) ÷ 2 = 30; 60 + 30 = 90.

image_decisions.why: The two base angles meeting at a corner show the 90° being built from the isosceles triangles.
